claim: Pimavanserin reduces psychosis in patients with Parkinson's disease
gold_rationale: Regulatory and clinical consensus support the claim. The pivotal 6-week phase 3 RCT (ACADIA Study-020, NCT01174004; Cummings et al., Lancet 2014, N=199) met its primary endpoint: pimavanserin 34 mg base (40 mg tartrate) reduced the Parkinson's-disease-adapted SAPS-PD by -3.06 vs placebo (95% CI -4.91 to -1.20; p=0.001; Cohen's d 0.50) WITHOUT worsening motor function (UPDRS II+III non-inferior, upper CI <=5). On the strength of this single positive pivotal trial plus supportive data (AdCom vote 12-2), the FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation (2014) and approved NUPLAZID on 29 April 2016 as the FIRST drug indicated for hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson's disease psychosis (PDP), at 34 mg/day. Independent meta-analyses of the PDP RCT program (Yasue 2016, 4 RCTs, 417 drug/263 placebo; Yunusa 2023 network MA, 19 studies/1,242 patients) confirm a statistically significant SAPS-H+D/SAPS-PD reduction with no motor deterioration. SAPS-PD is a validated clinical psychosis endpoint (not a surrogate), so the outcome matches the claim. Two caveats keep this short of dramatic/all-or-none: (1) the pooled effect is modest (d~0.5), driven largely by Study-020; (2) the drug carries a boxed warning for increased mortality in dementia-related psychosis, and the FDA did NOT approve the broader dementia-related-psychosis indication (HARMONY, NEJM 2021) despite a positive relapse-prevention trial. Within the specific PDP population and the SAPS-PD outcome, the verdict is Supported.
population: Parkinson's disease psychosis (hallucinations and/or delusions arising after PD diagnosis)
provenance: PubMed (with DOIs) + ClinicalTrials.gov + FDA (SEC 8-K/DailyMed/Drugs@FDA DRISK review) + Pharmaceutical Journal; independently re-verified via retrieval tools by the adversarial checker
notes: SAPS-PD is a validated clinical endpoint for PDP, not a surrogate (outcome_match=true across rows). Consensus is Supported specifically for PDP; the separate dementia-related-psychosis program (HARMONY) is a broader population, FDA-unapproved, and carries a mortality boxed warning — do not conflate. HARMONY's population_match=false is a correct honest call (broader population), not a wrongly-excluded conflicting PD trial. Effect is significant but modest (d~0.5), driven mainly by the single positive pivotal trial, so dramatic_effect=false everywhere. All rows re-verified against real sources; nothing dropped.

baseline.text: Yes. Pimavanserin (Nuplazid), a selective 5-HT2A inverse agonist, reduces psychosis in Parkinson's disease. Its pivotal 6-week phase 3 RCT (Cummings et al., Lancet 2014, N=199) showed a significant reduction in SAPS-PD scores versus placebo without worsening motor function, and the FDA approved it in 2016 as the first drug specifically for hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson's disease psychosis. Meta-analyses confirm the benefit. It carries a boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly dementia-related psychosis.

rows.citation: Cummings J, et al. Pimavanserin for patients with Parkinson's disease psychosis: a randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial. Lancet. 2014;383(9916):533-40. DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(13)62106-6 (NCT01174004, Study ACP-103-020).
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal registration trial; industry-funded (ACADIA); central independent SAPS-PD raters; 2-week non-pharmacological lead-in to limit placebo response. Verified: article types = Clinical Trial Phase III / RCT / Multicenter; NOT retracted.
rows.finding: Pimavanserin 40 mg tartrate/d reduced SAPS-PD by -5.79 vs -2.73 placebo (difference -3.06; 95% CI -4.91 to -1.20; p=0.001; Cohen's d 0.50), with no worsening of motor function (UPDRS II+III non-inferior). Landmark positive pivotal trial.

rows.citation: A Multi-Center, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Trial to Examine the Safety and Efficacy of Pimavanserin in the Treatment of Psychosis in Parkinson's Disease (ACADIA Study-020). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01174004. Phase 3, COMPLETED, N=199.
rows.integrity_note: Registry record for the pivotal trial; has_results=true; primary endpoint = change in SAPS-PD (9-item, 0-45) at Day 43; secondary UPDRS II+III non-inferiority (upper 95% CI <=5) met. Sponsor ACADIA. Verified against ClinicalTrials.gov.
rows.finding: Registry-level confirmation of the pivotal PDP trial: primary antipsychotic-efficacy endpoint (SAPS-PD reduction) met; motor non-inferiority (UPDRS II+III) demonstrated. Basis for FDA approval.

rows.citation: Tariot PN, Cummings JL, et al. Trial of Pimavanserin in Dementia-Related Psychosis (HARMONY). N Engl J Med. 2021;385(4):309-319. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2034634 (NCT03325556). PMID:34289275.
rows.integrity_note: Randomized-withdrawal (relapse-prevention) design; BROADER population (Alzheimer's, PD dementia, DLB, FTD, vascular) — includes but is not limited to PDP; stopped early for efficacy. FDA declined the dementia-related-psychosis indication. population_match=false verified as correct (broader population), NOT a mislabeled PDP trial.
rows.finding: Relapse of psychosis in 13% (12/95 pimavanserin) vs 28% (28/99 placebo); HR 0.35 (95% CI 0.17-0.73; p=0.005). Supports antipsychotic efficacy but in a broader dementia-related-psychosis population, not PDP specifically; FDA did not approve this indication.

rows.citation: Yasue I, et al. Serotonin 2A Receptor Inverse Agonist as a Treatment for Parkinson's Disease Psychosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. J Alzheimers Dis. 2016;50(3):733-40. DOI:10.3233/JAD-150818.
rows.integrity_note: Meta-analysis of 4 pimavanserin PDP RCTs (417 drug / 263 placebo); low heterogeneity (I2=30% for SAPS-H+D). Verified article type = Meta-Analysis / Systematic Review.
rows.finding: Pooled SAPS-H+D reduction WMD -2.26 (95% CI -3.86 to -0.67; p=0.005) favoring pimavanserin; significant on SAPS-H and SAPS-D; no motor worsening (UPDRS II+III); less orthostatic hypotension than placebo. Confirms modest but consistent benefit.

rows.citation: Yunusa I, et al. Comparative Efficacy, Safety, and Acceptability of Pimavanserin and Other Atypical Antipsychotics for Parkinson's Disease Psychosis: Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis. J Geriatr Psychiatry Neurol. 2023;36(5):417-432. DOI:10.1177/08919887231154933.
rows.integrity_note: Network meta-analysis, 19 studies / 1,242 PDP patients; one ACADIA-affiliated co-author (Rashid) — verified. Article type = Network Meta-Analysis / Systematic Review.
rows.finding: Pimavanserin and clozapine both significantly improved psychosis vs placebo (pimavanserin CGI-S SMD -4.81, 95% CI -5.39 to -4.24; SAPS OR 1.16, 95% CI 1.07-1.24) WITHOUT impairing motor function; quetiapine impaired cognition. Positions pimavanserin among preferred PDP agents.

rows.citation: Espay AJ, et al. Pimavanserin for Parkinson's Disease psychosis: Effects stratified by baseline cognition and use of cognitive-enhancing medications. Mov Disord. 2018;33(11):1769-1776. DOI:10.1002/mds.27488. PMID:30387904.
rows.integrity_note: Prespecified subgroup analysis of the pivotal NCT01174004 trial data (not an independent trial); industry-funded. Verified.
rows.finding: Antipsychotic effect on SAPS-PD robust across cognitive strata and larger in cognitively impaired PD (-6.62 vs -0.91 placebo; p=0.002); effect enhanced with concomitant cognitive-enhancing medication. Supports efficacy in the dementia-overlap PDP subgroup.

rows.citation: FDA approval of NUPLAZID (pimavanserin) for hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson's disease psychosis, 29 April 2016 (Breakthrough Therapy; NDA 207318; ACADIA Pharmaceuticals; AdCom 12-2). Reported: Pharmaceutical Journal 2016, DOI:10.1211/PJ.2016.20201108; corroborated by ACADIA SEC 8-K and FDA DailyMed/Drugs@FDA.
rows.integrity_note: US regulatory action based on the single pivotal Study-020 (NCT01174004) with supportive data; first-in-class approval at 34 mg/day. Carries a boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; NOT approved for dementia-related psychosis broadly. Verified via FDA/DailyMed and ACADIA 8-K.
rows.finding: FDA approved pimavanserin (34 mg/d) as the first drug indicated for hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson's disease psychosis, confirming regulatory consensus that it reduces PDP psychosis without worsening motor symptoms.
